title: Verbal Commitment Under Prior Credit Policy During Mid-Cycle Tightening
scenario_text:
**FIS Horizon — Pipeline Report (as of 11/15/2025)**
Loan #PENDING-2025-1134 | Borrower: Greystone Development Corp | Type: Construction-to-Perm | Amount: $8.5M | LTV: 78% | DSCR (projected): 1.18x | Status: Credit Memo in Progress
Relationship Manager: D. Parsons | Submitted to Credit: 10/28/2025

**SharePoint — Credit Policy Manual (Version 11.0, effective 11/01/2025)**
Section 3.2 — CRE Construction Lending:
'Maximum LTV for construction loans: 75%. Minimum DSCR (stabilized): 1.25x. No exceptions without Chief Credit Officer approval and documented mitigants.'
[Version History: v10.0 (effective 04/2023) stated: 'Maximum LTV: 80%. Minimum DSCR: 1.15x.']

**Outlook — Email Chain (10/22/2025)**
From: d.parsons@cascadefinancial.com
To: m.greystone@greystonedev.com
CC: t.whitfield@cascadefinancial.com
Subject: Cascade — Greystone Construction Facility

'Marcus — good speaking with you today. Per our discussion, we're pleased to confirm Cascade's interest in providing the $8.5M construction facility on the terms we discussed. I'll have the credit memo submitted by end of month. Formal commitment letter to follow after credit approval. Looking forward to partnering on this one.'

**Microsoft Teams — #cre-lending (10/30/2025, 11:22 AM)**
@d.parsons: Heads up — Greystone memo is in the queue. Tom gave verbal on this at 78% LTV back in October. Should be straightforward.
@j.chen: Policy 3.2 changed yesterday. New max LTV is 75% for construction. You aware?
@d.parsons: Wait what? That wasn't announced until the monthly.
@j.chen: Credit committee pushed it through 10/31 effective 11/1. The memo came out late Friday.
@d.parsons: We told the customer we'd do this. Tom was on the email.
@j.chen: 🤷‍♂️ talk to Tom

**SharePoint — Credit Committee Minutes (10/15/2025)**
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @cco.office, 10/29/2025]: 'Board approved tightening CRE parameters given market conditions. Transition guidance: loans with issued commitment letters prior to 11/1 are grandfathered. Pipeline deals without formal commitments subject to new policy.'

**Dynamics 365 — Relationship Notes (Greystone Development Corp)**
Entry (10/23/2025, D. Parsons): 'Verbal commitment extended per discussion with VP Whitfield. Customer expects formal CL within 3 weeks. Strong relationship — 3 prior deals closed, no losses. Greystone indicated competing term sheet from First National at 80% LTV.'

**Bloomberg Terminal — Market Data (pulled 11/10/2025)**
Greystone Development Corp — Private. No public filings.
Local CRE market (Charlotte MSA): Cap rate compression; office vacancy 14.2% (up from 11.8% YoY). Construction cost index +6.3% YTD.
question: Given the policy change, the verbal commitment, and the transition guidance in the credit committee minutes, what is the correct path for the Greystone $8.5M construction loan?

contributor.name: Thomas Whitfield
contributor.title: VP, Commercial Lending
contributor.domain_expertise: Loan origination, credit policy, covenant compliance, loan modifications, workout situations

choices: Honor the verbal commitment at 78% LTV — the email from 10/22 with a VP on CC constitutes an institutional commitment that predates the policy change
Apply new Policy 3.2 (75% LTV, 1.25x DSCR) — the transition guidance explicitly states only loans with issued commitment letters are grandfathered, and no commitment letter was issued
Approve at 78% LTV under the old policy since the credit memo was submitted on 10/28, one day before the new policy was approved by credit committee
Restructure to 75% LTV to comply with new policy but offer a rate concession to preserve the relationship, since the competing term sheet from First National makes this a retention risk
